note: SMAD2-related LDS6 shares core LDS craniofacial features with well-recognized ascertainment bias between severely presenting probands and cascade-tested relatives.

evidence.text: Loeys-Dietz syndrome manifests with cardinal features including hypertelorism and bifid/broad uvula or cleft palate, with SMAD2 identified as an intracellular effector involved in LDS exhibiting a broad emerging clinical spectrum.

source.title: A mutation update on the LDS‐associated genes TGFB2/3 and SMAD2/3
source.quote: Most typically, LDS patients present with aortic aneurysms and arterial tortuosity, hypertelorism, and bifid/broad uvula or cleft palate.

evidence.text: LDS is diagnosed across 6 genetic subtypes (including SMAD2 for LDS6) characterized by suggestive findings such as cleft palate and aortic dilatation, presenting a wide phenotypic spectrum.

source.title: Cleft Palate and Aortic Dilatation as Clues for Loeys–Dietz Syndrome
source.quote: Six different genes are involved in LDS and the diagnosis is based on the identification of a heterozygous pathogenic variant in TGFBR1, TGFBR2, SMAD3, TGFB2, TGFB3, or SMAD2 in children with suggestive findings.
